findings.description: hydrateDecisions() decodes a dehydrated payload's policy and entry envelope via decodePolicy (Schema.decodeUnknownOption(PolicySchema), line 43) and decodeEntryFields (Schema.decodeUnknownOption(DehydratedEntryFields), line 75) with no structural-depth pre-check, even though both traverse the same self-recursive Policy/Trace shapes (via Schema.suspend) that packages/core/src/Policy.ts's fromJson/fromJsonValue and packages/core/src/SinkCodec.ts's decodeRecordWire explicitly guard with exceedsJsonDepth before calling Schema. Policy.ts documents (MAX_DECODE_DEPTH comment) that Schema's own recursive descent through a suspended schema has no depth cap and raises a raw RangeError (confirmed empirically at ~60,000 levels, or as low as ~430 with onExcessProperty set) instead of a typed failure. DecodeDepthGuard.ts's own doc comment (lines 14-18) and SinkCodec.ts's decodeRecordWire doc comment (lines 606-607) both name this exact gap in Hydration.ts as 'tracked separately' but it is still unfixed. Confirmed that exceedsJsonDepth is not exported from packages/core/src/index.ts, so @qadi/react currently has no way to reach it even if it wanted to. A crafted dehydrated payload (e.g. embedded in a server-rendered page, which this module's own doc frames as 'authorization state crossing a network') nested past the stack limit throws a raw RangeError defect in the browser instead of the documented fail-closed 'drop the entry' behavior every other malformed-payload path in this module gets.
findings.suggestedFix: Export exceedsJsonDepth (and a suitable max-depth constant) from @qadi/core's public surface, then call it in hydrateDecisions before decodeEntryFields/decodePolicy — mirroring exactly the guard-then-decode order SinkCodec.ts's decodeRecordWire already uses — and drop the entry (counted/reported like the other four drop reasons) rather than let Schema recurse unbounded.

findings.description: decodeSinkRecordWireUnknown = Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(SinkRecordWire) (line 580) decodes with no ParseOptions, unlike packages/core/src/Policy.ts's UNTRUSTED_DECODE_OPTIONS ({ onExcessProperty: "error" }) used by every one of that file's untrusted entry points (decodePolicyUnknown, fromJson, fromJsonValue). SinkRecordWire embeds the same Policy schema (field `policy` on the Decision variant, line 186) and this file's own module doc comment (lines 13-18) frames decodeRecord as crossing the identical trust boundary ADR-QD-002 describes for Policy itself, quoting 'decodeRecord therefore validates; it does not cast.' Because onExcessProperty defaults to "ignore" in this Schema version (per Policy.ts's own MAX_DECODE_DEPTH-context comment), a wire-format record whose embedded policy has a typo'd field — e.g. {"_tag":"HasPermission","permision":...} — silently decodes with the permission grant absent rather than failing, which is exactly the 'silent data loss' class of defect ADR-QD-002 says the Policy ADT was rewritten to make unrepresentable. This decode path (used by decodeRecord/decodeRecordWire, reached by the devtools SSE reader in packages/devtools/src/model/Source.ts and any sink-forwarding consumer) currently bypasses that protection.
findings.suggestedFix: Export UNTRUSTED_DECODE_OPTIONS (or an equivalent) from Policy.ts and thread it into decodeSinkRecordWireUnknown = Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(SinkRecordWire, UNTRUSTED_DECODE_OPTIONS), matching Policy.ts's own stance for every other untrusted entry point that carries a Policy.

escalations: packages/core/src/FieldPath.ts's projectAt (used by Decision.ts's project, called on every field-restricted allow) is real function-call recursion with no depth guard, unlike every other recursive walk in this codebase's untrusted-input paths (Policy.ts's deepest, SinkCodec.ts's isJsonSafe, DecodeDepthGuard.ts's exceedsJsonDepth) which were deliberately converted to an explicit stack for exactly this reason. A policy's `fields`/visibleFields array (per ADR-QD-002, part of a Policy that is 'persisted and re-parsed from untrusted JSON') is split into dot-path segments by parseFieldPath with no length cap, and projectAt recurses once per matching segment against the resource being authorized. A crafted fields spec with enough dot-segments, combined with a resource whose shape nests correspondingly deep (plausible when resources are themselves arbitrary user-authored documents), can throw a raw RangeError out of the enforcement path itself — not just decode — potentially crashing the evaluating process rather than failing the one decision closed. This is a live authorization/evaluation-path crash rather than a decode-time one, so it looks like it could be Medium severity depending on how attacker-reachable the `fields` array and resource shape are in a given deployment.
